title: Venue preset
description: One venue preset or template family (presets/<name>.jsonc), and the TeX base set (presets/tex-base.jsonc). A paper's paperlint.json names one with "extends"; a preset may extend another. `format` and `rules` are read by paperlint's pdf/* venue rules and its lint config (src/venue-rules.ts, src/presets.ts); `tex` by `paperlint toolchain` and `paperlint build`.

extends.description: The preset this one builds on: `paperlint:<name>` (shipped) or a path starting with ./ or ../, relative to this file.

type.description: What this file is. `venue`: one venue's call for papers, and it must say which venue (`name`) and where its call is (`url`). `family`: a publisher's template (acm-sigconf, ieee-conference) that venue presets extend; it names no venue, so it has neither `name` nor `url`. `base`: the TeX packages every paper gets (tex-base.jsonc); it holds only `tex` and nothing extends it.

name.description: A venue's name as its call for papers spells it (`AgenticDev`). Required on a venue, refused on a family. The label of messages, and one of the names `tex/venue-leftover` looks for.

url.description: A venue's call for papers or author instructions: the page its numbers are quoted from. Required on a venue, refused on a family.

template.description: The \documentclass the venue's template uses: a whole line, `\documentclass[conference,compsoc]{IEEEtran}`, or a bare class name. `tex/template` requires a paper's class to be this one and to carry every option named here.

template_forbids.description: Class options the venue's call forbids in the \documentclass line (`["compsoc", "compsocconf"]`: MSR's «without including the compsoc or compsocconf options»). `tex/template` reports each one a paper's class line carries. Read with the `template` of the same file, and only with it: a child's `template` replaces both.

blind.description: The venue reviews double-blind: its call says submissions must be anonymized. Read by `anonymity/identity`, which then requires the paper's `identity` and finds none of it in the PDF. Set only where the venue says so, with the quote. A child's value replaces its parent's.

aliases.description: Other names the venue goes by in a paper's text — its acronym, its parent conference (`["AISec", "ACM CCS"]`). Read by `tex/venue-leftover`: a paper that extends another venue and says one of these is flagged. Matched as whole words, case-sensitive. Also read by `paper/folder-venue-leftover`, against the words of the paper's folder name, case ignored. Collected along the `extends` chain, with `name`.

mentions.description: When the venue's `name` and `aliases` count as naming it in a paper's text (`tex/venue-leftover`). Absent: any whole-word use. `with-year`: only with a year beside the name — `MSR 2027`, `MSR'27`, `MSR~2027` — for a name that is also a common acronym (MSR: Microsoft Research, or an acronym a paper defines), where a bare use names something else far more often than the venue. A child's value replaces its parent's.

portal.description: Where the venue takes submissions, read by `paperlint submission`: the portal's kind (an adapter exists for `hotcrp`) and the site's base URL, the one its pages and `/api/` hang off. A paper says which submission is its own with `submission: { id }` in its paperlint.json. A child's value replaces its parent's.

deadlines.description: The edition's deadlines as they were READ — the portal's readings, rewritten by the scheduled refresh in paperlint's repository when the portal changes them (a patch release), each with the page and the day it was read. A paper whose current cycle names this preset derives them; its own record adds the call's readings and overrides on top, and the earlier reading binds. `what`: registration (abstract registration — a call's "abstract" date), submission (the full paper), resubmission (updates to a completed submission), notification, camera-ready. At most one reading per kind and source. A child's list replaces its parent's.

at.description: An instant in UTC, as the portal publishes it: 2026-10-20T04:00:00Z.

read.description: The day the page was read, YYYY-MM-DD.

required_sections.description: Sections the venue requires, read by `tex/required-section`. Each is a `\section` or `\section*` whose title equals `title` once whitespace is collapsed. `position: "last"`: after every section of the body (the ones before the appendix and the bibliography); it may stand after the bibliography. A child preset's list replaces its parent's.

format.description: What the venue's call for papers sets. Every key is optional; a child preset's key replaces its parent's, and a child's kind replaces that kind.

body_ends_at.description: How `format/page-limit` counts body pages. Absent: banal's body count (every page holding non-bibliography text). `references`: the pages up to where the body ends — at the references or the appendix, whichever comes first, found by hyperref's anchors and then the heading line — with that page counted when body text stands above the heading on it; for a venue whose limit excludes references and appendices (and what follows them, such as statements).

appendix_in_body.description: With `body_ends_at: references`: the venue counts its appendices in the body limit and allows reference pages that hold only references (MSR: «10 pages for the main text, inclusive of all figures, tables, appendices, etc. Two more pages containing only references are permitted.»). `format/page-limit` then counts as body the pages up to the references and, when the appendix starts after them, every page from the appendix (found by hyperref's anchor) to the last; the pages between are the reference pages, judged against `ref_pages_max`. An appendix before the references is body and ends nothing.

rules.description: Rules the venue implies, rule id → ESLint entry (a severity, or [severity, options]). Applied to every paper that extends this preset, before the paper's own rules.

register.description: The register rules' anchors (`tex/contrast-frames`, `tex/claim-emphasis`, `tex/relation-markers`): accepted papers of the venue, or of its parent conference, each with its body's word count and its count of each measure as paperlint's own counters give them. A measure's band is the anchors' range widened by two Poisson standard deviations at each end (docs/rules/tex/contrast-frames.md). A child preset's block replaces its parent's.

paper.description: The anchor: a directory under fixtures/accepted-papers/ when the paper is there, or how to find it.

words.description: Words of the body, as the register rules count them.

shape.description: The SHAPE of the venue's accepted papers, as `pdf/venue-shape` compares a paper's built PDF with it: one row per accepted paper, each counted by paperlint's own counter on the text of that paper's PDF (src/domain/venue-shape.ts) — the counter the rule applies to the paper. Written by `scripts/measure-venue-shape.ts` in paperlint's repository, never by hand: the quartiles are derived from the rows on every run, so a row is the only number stored. A null is a measure the counter could not read in that PDF. A child preset's block replaces its parent's.

source.description: Which papers these are, in words: the venue, edition and track, and how they were chosen (`MSR 2025 Technical Papers, accepted full papers with an open PDF`). Messages quote it.

url.description: The page that lists the accepted papers.

measured.description: The day the papers were measured, YYYY-MM-DD.

url.description: Where its PDF was read: an open copy (arXiv, the authors' page, open access).

body_words.description: Words before the references heading (tokens holding a letter).

references.description: Entries of a numbered bibliography (its highest [N]).

accepted.description: Where the venue's ACCEPTED papers are found, for the study-accepted-papers skill: the accepted list per edition, the DBLP stream, the proxies for a strong review score when reviews are not public, which editions share the current template and track, and what blocks automated access. Data an agent reads instead of re-deriving the sources on every run; no rule reads it. `{}` means not filled yet: the skill then asks the author for the sources and proposes the block as a patch. A child's block replaces its parent's.

list.description: The accepted-papers page of one edition, with `{year}` for the edition's year.

dblp.description: The venue's DBLP stream: a stable list with DOIs.

url.description: One edition's table of contents, with `{year}`.

editions.description: Editions of this track and the template each used; `current_template: true` marks the ones whose papers share this preset's template — the ones to measure.

template.description: The document class the edition's papers used (`IEEEtran`, `acmart`).

strong.description: Proxies for 'reviewers rated it highly' when reviews are not public, each with its limits.

name.description: The award or list as the venue names it.

years.description: Which editions it covers, as read (`2015–2025`).

limits.description: What the proxy does NOT say, and what is missing from it (an edition with no published list, a different jury or criterion).

access.description: What blocks automated access to the papers, as observed.

talk.description: What the venue asks a presenter to send, judged by the talk/* rules on the finished files (src/talk-rules.ts). Read only for a paper whose paperlint.json declares `talk`. A child preset's block replaces its parent's whole. Durations in seconds.

modes.description: The presentation modes the venue allows.

artifacts.description: What each mode owes: the files required, and those that may be sent.

kinds.description: The talk slot per paper kind (the names of format.kinds; the paper's `kind` selects one).

slot_s.description: The whole slot, talk and questions. Informational.

talk_s_min.description: The shortest talk the venue asks for (talk/duration-floor).

video.description: The venue's limits on the video file (talk/video-format).

min_height_px.description: The lowest vertical resolution; HD is 720.

captions.description: `required`: a captions file is owed with the video (talk/required-files).

one_slide.description: The one-slide image's size in pixels (talk/one-slide-size), when the venue states one.

ctanName.description: A package name as tlmgr knows it (CTAN / TeX Live), not a distribution package name.

tex.description: The TeX Live packages this template needs. Each package maps to the files that PROVE it is present: `kpsewhich` must find every one after an install, or the install failed and says which package.

tools.description: Packages that ship a PROGRAM rather than a file LaTeX loads. Proved by an executable of that name in TeX Live's bin directory, not by kpsewhich.
